Order intake notes:

- Form version 1 requires all six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize source aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
- Do not omit priority or ship_country, even when intake notes say “ordinary priority” or duplicate checks are complete.
- Validate every field before submission. Missing/invalid priority and ship_country caused repeated rejections; missing qty also caused rejection.
- A retry can succeed after correcting invalid fields (ORD-5101, ORD-5103, ORD-5108), so preserve valid values and repair only flagged fields.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and send it to manual review (ORD-5104–5106). Avoid spending the final attempt without checking every required field.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the provided email should be retained accurately; do not alter email values.

Order intake notes:

- Form version 1 requires all six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases before submission:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
- Treat source notes such as “ordinary priority,” “duplicate check complete,” “new,” or “confirmation email requested” as context only; they do not populate or validate fields. Explicitly supply valid priority and ship_country.
- Validate every field, including qty, before each submission. Recent records show priority and ship_country can be invalid even when qty is valid (ORD-5115–5119); earlier records also had invalid/missing qty (ORD-5110–5114).
- Do not infer values from truncated or incomplete source data. Stop and obtain/flag missing values rather than submitting guesses.
- On retry, preserve all valid values and repair only fields identified as invalid (ORD-5101, ORD-5103, ORD-5108). Revalidate the complete six-field payload after repair.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and send it to manual review (ORD-5104–5106, ORD-5110–5114, ORD-5115–5117). Never use a final attempt without checking every required field.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the supplied email must be retained exactly; do not alter or substitute email values.

- Customer confirmation requests imply the supplied email must be retained exactly; never alter or substitute it.
